newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa, British Midland in cooperation talks.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa, British Midland in cooperation talks.

text.p: Deutsche Lufthansa AG said it is negotiating with British Midland on a possible cooperation agreement but declined to give further details.

A Lufthansa spokeswoman commenting on German press reports told Reuters: "It is clear that negotiations are taking place with British Midland. Lufthansa will say nothing further till a strike ballot by (Lufthansa white-collar staff) is completed on February 25."
The spokeswoman declined to say whether the talks covered only flights and code-sharing or could involve a Lufthansa shareholding in the British carrier.

Lufthansa chairman Juergen Weber was quoted by German travel trade publication FVW International on Friday as saying: "We are negotiating with British Midland to build up a presence in Great Britain."
"As part of this cooperation, should the alliance happen, part of our UK services will be flown by British Midland," Weber added.
The deal was a response to the planned British Airways and American Airlines alliance and expansion of domestic services by Deutsche BA, Weber said.
Another German trade magazine said the negotiations included a possible 40 percent Lufthansa stake in the UK carrier.
Lufthansa financial director Klaus Schlede told Reuters last May the German airline was interested in a financial involvement in the UK carrier.
British Midland is a subsidiary of Airlines of Britain Holding, in which Scandinavian Airlines System has a 40 percent stake.

The Lufthansa-based global alliance with SAS, United Airlines, Thai Airways International and South African Airways (SAA.CN) is gradually building up a network of mutual code-sharing agreements, industry observers noted.
